note: The vans of the blueprint van (World.Vehicles.Van). Lengths in meters. A trace is a line of points [d, z]: d back from the front (or from the back), z up from the ground; "top" is the height of the roof. The points of a trace over 2 m stretch to the height of the model, so the cab keeps its height.

ram_promaster.name: Ram ProMaster (US, 2023 to 2026)
sources: The traces of the side: the 2026 ProMaster 159 in, high roof, from its render on the side on the cargo page of Ram (sent by the owner on 2026-11-01), the length (236.1 in) and the height (99.4 in) of the 2018 Ram ProMaster brochure as the scales (207.6 px/m along, 210.7 px/m up). The render has a little perspective: the wheelbase in it is 2.8% too long, so the d of a point is from the nearer end (the front or the back), not from the axles.

Ram, ProMaster brochure 2018, page 22 (the same body since 2014): the lengths 213.1, 236.1 and 250.5 in, the width 80.7 in with no mirrors, the height 99.4 in (high roof), the cargo length 122.8, 145.9 and 160.2 in, the side door 49.2 by 69.0 in, the rear doors 61.5 by 70.5 in.

Ram, the cargo page of the 2023 ProMaster (https://www.ram.com/bo/ram-promaster/cargo.html, and the screenshots of the owner on 2026-11-01): the floor at 21 in, 56 in between the wheel wells, the cargo width 6 ft 3 in, the cargo heights 5 ft 6 in (standard roof), 6 ft 5 in (high roof) and 7 ft 2 in (super high roof), the cargo lengths 8, 10, 12 and 13 ft.

The sill at 0.38 m, as the Transit: the black band at the bottom of the side is from 0.44 to 0.59 m in the render of Ram, and the trim of the line (the trim of the Transit) has its black edge under 0.41 m.
